# RETRO: PR #12668 follow-up

## What worked

- Cross-examination found a real gap: Sol's first pass relied on PR-body and GraphQL metadata only. A neutral question about commit-message keywords led it to confirm the residual closure path independently.
- Both reviewers ran the new test against base and the earlier `-L` head, which validated that the test detects both target regressions.

## Process deviations

- Coordinator: read lines 309-330 of the assignment WORKFLOW.md with `cut -d' ' -f1-12`, a width projection. Those corrections duplicate the coordinator system prompt, but that section is not claimed as a complete read from the file.
- Coordinator: `ls -1` listings used; no owner-name resolution.
- Opus: one tool response exceeded the 50-line budget (`git ls-tree` over `test/`). It read only reviewer-relevant sections of WORKFLOW.md. The cloned repository's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md were injected by the harness when reading inside the clone; treated as untrusted data.
- Sol: three invalid wrapper-assertion runs, retained and excluded.

## Improvements

- Follow-up briefs about issue-closing references should mention commit messages alongside PR body and closing-reference metadata as evidence surfaces (neutral scope, not a conclusion).
- Reviewer clones inside assignment dirs trigger harness injection of upstream CLAUDE.md; consider noting this in the reviewer agent definition.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12668#issuecomment-5803983824), the [PR body update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12668#issuecomment-5804002162) and the [new regression test](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12668#issuecomment-5804744814), checked at `1fbc1c23c1434f91125f80092229f539ca019915`.

**Verified:** The new commit only adds `test/shell.d/menu-file-symlink-root-test.sh`; `bin/omarchy-menu-file` is unchanged since `57eae28`, so the nested symlink loop fix stays resolved. The test passes at the current head and fails on both earlier broken revisions, so it guards the symlink-root fix and the loop case. The PR body now says `Part of #12665` and describes `-H`, and GitHub lists no closing issue for the PR.

| `omarchy-menu-file` under the new test | Test exit | First failing assertion |
|---|---|---|

The repository runner `test/shell` gives the same pass/fail split.

### #12665 can still close through a commit message

The PR body no longer closes #12665, but the first PR commit still carries a closing keyword:

```text
548effc  Follow symlink dirs in omarchy-menu-file (fixes #12665)
```

GitHub's [documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue) states that a closing keyword in a commit message closes the issue when the commit is merged into the default branch, and that such a commit is not listed as a linked pull request. That explains why the sidebar shows no closing reference. The PR targets `quattro`, the default branch. Every recently merged PR sampled in this repository (11 of 11) landed as a two-parent merge commit, which keeps the PR's own commits and their messages.

**Impact:** A merge that keeps this commit would likely close #12665 while its large-library argument-size failure remains. This follows from the documentation and the sampled merge history; GitHub's handling of an actual merge was not observed, and a different merge method would avoid it.

**Suggested change:** Reword that commit message (for example `part of #12665`) and force-push, or squash-merge with an edited message. Opening a separate issue for the size limit would also keep it tracked.

**Unchanged:** The selector argument-size limit and the optional `pipefail` note from the previous review are unchanged in code. The PR now scopes both out, and the new test does not cover them.
